accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE 2013 Years 3–4 English programme of study (recognise some different forms of poetry such as free verse and narrative poetry; prepare poems to read aloud and perform, showing understanding through intonation, tone, volume and action) and CCSS RL.4.5 and RF.3.4b. Haiku is given as 5-7-5 syllables in English, narrative poems as poems that tell a story (Noyes' The Highwayman, Browning's The Pied Piper), and free verse as poetry without regular rhyme or metre.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the common Key Stage 2 beliefs that a poem must rhyme (first prediction and tag rhyme), that syllables are letters or words (haiku clapping, tag count), that only funny poems tell stories (narrative step, tag story) and that performing means reading fast and loud (performance step, tag voice).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagpoem sorts poems by form, fills a 3 by 3 feature chart, claps a haiku line by line and repairs the middle line with sil-ver, finds the beginning, problem and end of the narrative poem Tom and the Boat, and tunes volume, pace and intonation on a waveform with listener reactions. No other lab models syllable counts or performance, and the shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners see each idea before it is stated: the free verse card is accepted as a poem without rhyme, the clap counter shows 6 beats on the middle line until sil-ver makes 7, the story strip lights up beginning, problem and end, and the listeners only lean in when pace slows and intonation rises at the question.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with plausible wrong options: is a poem without rhyme still a poem, how many syllables the middle haiku line needs (5 is tempting), and how to perform a tense moment (fast and loud is tempting). A.reveal repeats the learner's guess beside the outcome.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Rotating challenge tagged count, story, rhyme, voice and q; why() explains each slip, for example syllables are beats you clap, not letters, and a question rises at the end. Answer order rotates.

readability.evidence: Learner audience for ages 7–10: kid text scores about 1.3 and adult text about 6.2 on the FK check, both well inside the limits, and use exact Year 3–4 terms: free verse, narrative poem, haiku, syllable, rhyme, stanza, intonation, volume and pace.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate passed and overlap with other English lessons, including rhyme and story-structure lessons, is under 12 percent. Each paragraph adds one form or one performance skill, and the adult text names the mistakes and gives a home routine for reading poems aloud.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 light and Android dark screenshots after every Show me: the feature chart fits 3 by 3 with Yes and No in each cell, haiku lines and clap dots fit the width, and the waveform and listener icons sit clear of the controls. Every action has a full-width button twin.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed after fixing the chart Show me (cells meant to be No now land on No): axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, no console errors, all Show me tasks completed. The canvas aria-label speaks each clap count and performance result in words, not colour alone.
